Interview experience  
 
 
Name: Shardul Khade 
VJTI CE 2021-25 
Job Location: Navi Mumbai 
Job Role: Data Engineer 
 
Process : 
 
• PPT 
• OA 
• Interviews 
 
➢ Pay attention to ppt. It is one of the most important resources when you are appearing 
for the interview.  
 
Round 1 - OA: 20th Oct 2024: 4pm to 5pm 
- 2 coding problems  
1. Bob has a special chess board of size M X N. Cell (1,1) is at top left comer. If one of his 
bishops is placed at the cell (x,y), what is the maximum number of cells P he can cover in & 
moves, Bishop can walk through only diagonal cells and can walk any number of cells (till 
the boundary of the board) at one move diagonally. 
Read the input from STDIN and print the output to STDOUT. Do not write arbitrary strings 
while reading the input or while printing, as these contribute to the standard output. 
1<=M,N<=1000 
L<=15

Input M, N, x, y, L; 
Output: P 
 
Sample Input:  
5 6 2 3 4 
Sample output: 15 
I passed 8/12 tc. 
 
2. Given a 2D Matix (MxN) with each cell labelled serially ie. 1,2,3..MxN  
 
Print row wise all the cell numbers(serial no. allocated to cells). New row in new line. 
 I had solved it completely but it was printing an extra space at the end of last output char, 
did not get any time to debug hence 0/12 passed. 
 
 I thought I will not get an interview but apparently many people faced time constraint and 
could not solve much. I was shortlisted for the interviews. 
 
Interviews:  23rd Oct 2024, TPO VJTI

Round 2: Technical – 45mins  
There were 6 people shortlisted. I was called in second for my first interview around 10:45 
AM. The interviewer was polite. He asked me to introduce myself and briefly describe all my 
projects. After discussing one project in detail, he moved on to SQL questions. 
 
He asked me to write any SQL query to check if I understood the syntax. I wrote a simple 
query using a WHERE clause. 
 
Then he asked: 
• A query using GROUP BY 
• What is a HAVING clause? 
• The execution order of SQL queries 
Given a table (Name, primary_phone_no, sec_phone_no), I had to return the name and phone 
number, using the secondary number if the primary number was NULL. I answered using 
CASE IF. 
He then presented a schema with two tables. I was asked to find the count of each product 
and display it in separate columns (like colA, colB...) with just one row. I used GROUP BY 
but couldn't pivot the rows. He kept asking if I could write a simpler query. I said I didn’t 
know how. 
He asked if I knew about Window functions in SQL. I honestly said no, although I had heard 
of them. He said that was fine. He asked if I had worked with ETL/Big Data tools. I 
mentioned I had only heard of Informatica. He also asked about Power BI, which I hadn’t 
used. 
 
More questions: 
1. What are the different types of relationships in DB schema (e.g., one-to-one, one-to-
many)? Give examples. 
2. What is a foreign key? What is a primary key? 
3. Difference between UNION and UNION ALL? 
4. Given department and employee tables, find department-wise average employee 
salary. 
 
At the end, he asked a situational question: How would you handle working with someone 
difficult 
He then asked what I expected from the job at Mastercard—money, work-life balance, or 
growth. I said I was focused on learning and growth, explaining that since I had no major 
family responsibilities, money or WLB wasn't a priority. He was impressed. He asked if I had 
any questions for him (always prepare thoughtful questions).

Round 3: Technical - 30mins 
Immediately after, I was called for the second round, which was virtual. A GMeet was 
set up in the interview cabin. The interviewer was from the Pune office. She was 
polite and ensured I was comfortable. She introduced herself and described their work 
and tech stack. 
(Side note: Pay attention to such details. Don’t ask questions later that were already 
answered in the PPT or by the interviewer.) 
She asked: 
• 
What am I doing in my final year project? 
• 
How would I manage and schedule tasks in a large project to ensure I don’t miss 
deadlines? 
I answered using my FYP as an example, breaking down tasks into milestones and 
referencing SDLC concepts. She seemed satisfied. 
She then asked me to write an SQL query. It was a bit complex, and I had to explain it 
over video. I wasn’t sure, but I walked her through my thought process, and it turned 
out correct. 
She asked the same question as the previous interviewer: "Can you simplify it? Heard 
of window functions?" At this point, I realized it was an important topic. I told her I 
had heard of them but didn’t know how to use them. She said that was fine. 
The query involved a table with appliance details, categories, and transaction data. I 
had to return the top 5 grossing appliances in each category, which involved nested 
GROUP BYs. 
This round helped me understand the importance of trusting your gut and thinking out 
loud. 
She repeated the teamwork question from the first round about handling difficult 
colleagues. Then she asked if I had any questions. I asked the same ones as before: 
1. How long have you been working here, and how has your role evolved since the first 
week? 
2. What advice would you give to a fresher to ensure growth? 
3. Is there anything in my resume you found concerning or that I should improve? 
 
Round 4: HR (15 mins) 
 
I was immediately informed I was selected for the HR round. I didn’t even get a chance to 
talk to other candidates. Later, I found out I was the first and only one selected for HR. 
 
She asked me for a brief introduction and explicitly asked if there was anything I wanted her 
to know. I mentioned my hobbies and childhood background. She asked about my family. I 
shared that my sister is pursuing medicine, that sparked a question regarding my plans for 
higher studies. I told them- I don’t want to spend more time studying. I always wanted to start 
implementing what I learn and learn on the go.

She asked how many interviews I had appeared for and in how many I had reached the HR 
round. I said 3-4 companies and reached the last round in all of them. She asked why I wasn’t 
getting offers. I said I wasn’t sure, but I had reflected on it. I gave an example of ,y SAP Labs 
interview, where I cleared all four rounds (2 tech + 2 HR) but didn’t receive an offer. I 
speculated that maybe I didn’t convince them I was open to relocating to Bangalore. She 
smiled and said that wouldn’t be an issue now since the posting is in Navi Mumbai. I replied 
that Bangalore wasn’t a problem either, but this location was ideal as it’s just 20 minutes 
from my home. 
After the interview, I was asked to stay on campus for results. By 12:30 PM, all my rounds 
were done. Around 4 PM, I received a call from the TPO CR and was called to the TPO 
office. They announced that I was being offered the role. 
 
It felt surreal. Everything that could go right, did go right. The day before, I was interviewing 
with another company and was almost selected, but they added another round the next day. 
That allowed me to attend Mastercard's interview. Had I been selected by the previous 
company, I might have missed this opportunity. 
 
It was a long and tough placement season, but finally securing an offer felt like all the hard 
work paid off. 
 
Words of Wisdom: 
Take every rejection as an opportunity to level up. Make sure you hit every next opportunity 
harder than the last. Be ready—things move fast once they start happening. Work hard; 
there’s no way around it. Don’t buy into luck stories (although luck matters, you can’t rely on 
it—what you can control is your effort). 
 
All the best!
